To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) music application domains and music metadata schemas are both described by a cluster of metadata fields; (2) the metadata field clusters of the application domains and metadata schema are compared to find the most appropriate schema for a certain application domain; and (3) a decision table is presented to help the user of a music metadata provider in choosing a metadata schema

(1) metadata schemas can be linked with music applications by using metadata field clusters, (2) the metadata schemas and the application domains can be linked using the decision table, (3) the decision table can help users in choosing a suitable metadata schema for a specific application.
(1) music applications make use of the clusters of metadata fields to different degrees, and (2) different metadata schemas are better suited to different application domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mapping of metadata schemas to application domains, which can be used as a guide for music application developers.
the mapping of music metadata schemas to application domains.

the mapping between metadata schemas and application domains, and how this mapping could assist the music metadata provider in choosing an appropriate metadata schema for an intended application domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no one size fits all solution, but that the user should be aware of all possibilities.
there is no single metadata schema that can be used for all music application domains.

the music application domain of music recommendation has a high overlap with the metadata schemas MusicBrainz and MusicIP, while the music application domain for music search has a higher overlap with the metadata schema MusicBrainz.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a metadata schema is a good fit for an application domain if the schema covers the functionality space of the domain and the metadata fields in the schema are used to describe the domain.
the metadata schema Musicbrainz is the most complete and expressive metadata schema.
the presented approach helps to connect the dots between music metadata schemas, metadata field clusters, and music application domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expressiveness and the richness of a metadata field can vary significantly.
the expressiveness of a music metadata schema is not only determined by the number of metadata fields, but also by how these metadata fields are related to each other.
the metadata schema should be chosen carefully to ensure a good fit for the application domain.
